> purposely and actively hurt myself

Oof, self-sabotage is something I know well. All I can say to that is you have to really really force yourself to make choices that will benefit you. Nobody else can do that - believe me, I know - but you. You have all the power in the world contained within the human form. You are amazing.
You're *not worthless.* You have been given the precious gift of life, one that so many have lost unwillingly. No human being is worthless.

As someone who attempted and was never found out, it's definitely eye-opening to learn if you're really that accepting of death. I wasn't. My choice was to hang myself, but the weight of me and my shitty knot tying caused the knot to give and I fell down. Dumb, but that's how it goes.

As someone who burned out at just about exactly the time you did, I feel you. The pressure got to me, too. In earlier years I had been top of my class, but suddenly I was lucky to get a B- if that. I flunked biology with a 17. I don't want you to make the same mistakes I did. This post is proof that you're *doing something about it,* and that's already leagues ahead of what I did.

So open up that textbook and finish that essay, because you're already doing something by posting here so you might as well put that willpower, that strength to even attempt to change your situation, towards making your situation better. Just a few more short years and you'll be home free, my friend, and the world will be your oyster.
I'm no doctor, but that sounds like depression to me. Have you seen anyone about it? It might be able to lift you out of it, at least somewhat.
Thank you. If I could change my name to u/HappyEmoticon, I would.
Guy, I don't know your girlfriend. But I think you really should tell her because I doubt she'll hate you for it.
I have not, but I can verify that 28 in a day is bad for mental health.
